p.seg: Considering them to be groundless fabrications (xūdàn).
At this time, after Emperor Líng (靈帝) died,
Only Jiāozhōu (交州) was comparatively peaceful.
People from the north (běifāng), various and unusual, all came and resided there.
Many practiced the arts of divine immortals, abstaining from grain (pìgǔ), and achieving longevity (chángshēng).
Many people of the time became their followers.
Múzi often used the Five Classics (Wǔjīng) to challenge them.
No Daoist (Dàojiā) practitioners (shùshì) dared to respond.
(His efforts were) comparable to those of Mèng Kē (孟軻, Mencius) in refuting Yáng Zhū (楊朱) and Mò Dí (墨翟, Mozi).
Before this time, Múzi, with his mother (mǔ), had fled the world (bìshì) to Jiāozhǐ (交趾).
At twenty-six years old, he returned to Cāngwú (蒼梧) and married a wife.
The Administrator heard of his dedication to learning (shǒuxué).
(The Administrator) formally requested to appoint him as an official (lì).
